title: Weekly Buzz: SNY, REGN Score Approvals; MIST Cuts Costs; ABBV, LLY, JNJ Strike Deals - RTTNews
content: This week's biotech roundup features significant regulatory milestones, corporate restructuring and strategic dealmaking, alongside clinical developments across oncology, neurology, and rare diseases. Sanofi and Regeneron secured FDA approvals for therapies targeting neurological complications of rare and autoimmune diseases, while Revolution Medicines gained EU authorization for its pancreatic cancer drug. Summit Therapeutics, however, faced an FDA setback for ivonescimab. Meanwhile, Milestone Pharmaceuticals announced workforce and cost-reduction measures, major pharmaceutical companies pursued acquisitions and collaborations, and clinical trial updates highlighted promising survival benefits, Alzheimer's disease data and advances in osteoarthritis treatment. Sanofi (SNY) secured FDA approval for Infilbray (venglustat), the first therapy specifically indicated for neurological manifestations of Type 3 Gaucher disease in adults and children weighing at least 15 kg. The approval was supported by the Phase 3 LEAP2MONO trial, which met its primary endpoint at Week 52, demonstrating significant improvement in neurological symptoms versus imiglucerase. Infilbray received FDA Breakthrough Therapy, Fast Track, Rare Pediatric Disease and Priority Review designations. SNY closed Thursday's trading (November 19, 2026) at $46.06, down 2.25% Regeneron Pharmaceuticals (REGN) secured FDA approval for Livsayis (cemdisiran), the first siRNA therapy for adults with anti-AChR antibody-positive generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG). It is administered subcutaneously four times a year. The approval was supported by the Phase 3 NIMBLE trial, in which Livsayis demonstrated a 2.3-point placebo-adjusted improvement in MG-ADL scores at Week 24. This marks Regeneron's first approved neurology medicine and siRNA therapy. REGN closed Thursday's trading at $923.34, down 2.35% Revolution Medicines (RVMD) secured European Commission approval for RASONQUE (daraxonrasib), an oral RAS-targeted therapy for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), across all EU and EEA member states. The drug will be available as a monotherapy. The approval was supported by the Phase 3 RASolute 302 trial, which demonstrated statistically significant improvements in progression-free survival and overall survival. RASONQUE previously received FDA approval on August 26, 2026. RVMD closed Thursday's trading at $159.43, down 0.24% Summit Therapeutics (SMMT) received an FDA Complete Response Letter (CRL) for its BLA seeking approval of ivonescimab, in combination with platinum-based chemotherapy, for EGFR-mutated locally advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) following EGFR-targeted therapy. The FDA said the Phase 3 HARMONi trial failed to demonstrate statistically significant overall survival improvements, noting that progression-free survival benefit alone was insufficient to support approval. Ivonescimab was previously approved in China in May 2024. SMMT closed Thursday's trading at $10.57, up 0.67% Milestone Pharmaceuticals (MIST) announced restructuring measures, including reductions in headquarters personnel and workforce costs, as part of a plan to cut operating expenses by approximately 30%. CFO Amit Hasija and CMO David Bharucha also departed, with Bharucha transitioning to an advisory role. The measures are expected to result in approximately $2 million in one-time charges, primarily related to severance and workforce reductions, and extend the company's cash runway into late 2028. MIST closed Thursday's trading at $0.39, down 13.27% VivoSim Labs (VIVS) signed a seven-figure agreement with a top-10 global pharmaceutical company to provide liver and intestinal toxicology testing services through its NAMkind platforms, with testing already underway. The deal is expected to drive fiscal 2027 revenue growth beyond the company's previous guidance of more than 500%. VIVS closed Thursday's trading at $0.29, up 142.92% AbbVie (ABBV) partnered with privately held DISCO Pharmaceuticals to discover and develop AND-gated bispecific therapies for solid tumors, combining DISCO's DISCOtech cancer-cell surface mapping platform with AbbVie's oncology expertise. DISCO will receive $40 million upfront and is eligible for up to $2.5 billion in milestone payments, plus tiered royalties on worldwide net sales. ABBV closed Thursday's trading at $283.54, down 0.86% Eli Lilly (LLY) agreed to acquire privately held Calytrix Bio for up to $1.5 billion in cash, including upfront and milestone-based payments, to advance an investigational preclinical antibody targeting mutant calreticulin in essential thrombocythemia and myelofibrosis. The acquisition adds Calytrix's biparatopic antibody program, designed to selectively target disease-driving mutant cells, to Lilly's blood cancer pipeline. LLY closed Thursday's trading at $1,351.12, down 2.29% Biogen (BIIB) and Eisai (4523.T) reported three-year real-world data from the ongoing LEADER study, showing that LEQEMBI (lecanemab) was associated with a 75% lower rate of progression to moderate or severe Alzheimer's disease dementia compared with a matched external control group. The analysis included 560 patients across 13 U.S. sites. Additionally, 81.1% of evaluable patients remained stable or improved, while 77% achieved amyloid-negative status after a median follow-up of approximately 18 months. BIIB closed Thursday's trading at $247.13, down 1.70% Bristol Myers Squibb (BMY) reported preliminary positive data from the open-label periods of its Phase 3 ADEPT program evaluating KarXT (xanomeline and trospium chloride) for psychosis associated with Alzheimer's disease. In ADEPT-1, 273 patients showed a mean 12-point reduction in hallucination and delusion scores, with low treatment discontinuation rates. KarXT is already approved in the U.S. for schizophrenia and is marketed under the brand name Cobenfy. BMY closed Thursday's trading at $58.34, down 2.05% Enlivex (ENLV) reported positive 12-month results from its Phase I/IIa trial of Allocetra, an investigational cell-based therapy for moderate to severe knee osteoarthritis. Among patients aged 64 and older, 79.2% receiving Allocetra showed reduced pain and improved knee function, compared with 47.6% on placebo. The 134-patient trial showed sustained benefits after a single treatment cycle of three knee injections, with no treatment-related serious adverse events. Enlivex expects Phase IIb topline results by the end of Q2 2027. ENLV closed Thursday's trading at $1.17, down 2.50% SELLAS Life Sciences (SLS) reported positive results from its Phase 3 REGAL trial evaluating cancer vaccine candidate Galinpepimut-S (GPS) as maintenance therapy in patients with relapsed acute myeloid leukemia (AML) who achieved a second or later remission but were ineligible for stem cell transplantation. The trial met its primary endpoint, with GPS reducing the risk of death by 41% versus best available treatment. Median overall survival was 24 months versus 14.7 months. SELLAS plans to discuss an accelerated FDA filing pathway and prepare a BLA submission in H1 2027. SLS closed Thursday's trading at $14.86, down 17.21% Halozyme Therapeutics (HALO) plans to file a patent infringement lawsuit against Merck (MRK) in Germany seeking a permanent ruling over Keytruda SC, after a German appeals court overturned a preliminary injunction that had barred its distribution and sale. The dispute centers on Halozyme's MDASE drug-delivery patent portfolio. Separately, a Dutch court ruling restricting Keytruda SC commercialization in several European countries remains in place. HALO closed Thursday's trading at $93.04, down 2.88% Beren Therapeutics' subsidiary Mandos secured FDA approval for Lembaz (adrabetadex), the first therapy shown to extend survival in adults and children weighing at least 7 kg with infantile-onset Niemann-Pick disease type C (NPC). The approval was supported by data from 36 treated patients, showing a 55% reduction in the risk of death and median survival of 8.5 years versus 4.9 years in a matched external control group. Johnson & Johnson is reportedly considering acquiring privately held Ollin Biosciences in a deal valued at up to $3.4 billion, including a potential $2.2 billion upfront payment and $1.2 billion in milestone payments, according to the Financial Times. Ollin's pipeline includes OLN324 for diabetic macular edema and wet age-related macular degeneration, and OLN102 for thyroid eye disease and Graves' disease. The discussions are ongoing, and a deal is not yet certain. JNJ closed Thursday's trading at $267.14, down 2.04% The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) issued an epidemiological alert on November 17, 2026, highlighting the start of the 2026-2027 seasonal influenza period in the Northern Hemisphere. The agency called for enhanced surveillance of influenza and other respiratory viruses, timely vaccination and improved healthcare system preparedness as seasonal activity increases. title: Abbott Laboratories (NYSE: ABT), AbbVie (NYSE: ABBV), And Coca-Cola (NYSE: KO) Stand Out As Elite Dividend Compounders Built To Last - Foreign Policy Journal
content: By David Prior | Nov 19, 2026 | Economy & Business, Featured, News & Analysis Abbott Laboratories (NYSE: ABT) made headlines this year after closing a $21 billion cash deal to acquire Exact Sciences, a company focused on cancer diagnostics. The acquisition targets one of Abbott’s slower-growing business units and signals a strategic push to strengthen its diagnostic capabilities in an increasingly competitive healthcare market. Abbott also leads the continuous glucose monitoring space through its FreeStyle Libre franchise, giving it a meaningful foothold in one of medical technology’s fastest-expanding categories. Despite a stretch of mediocre financial results and lingering legal and regulatory headaches, the company’s dividend growth streak remains intact, and analysts see little reason to expect that to change anytime soon. AbbVie (NYSE: ABBV), which was carved out of Abbott as a standalone public company in 2013, has built a compelling track record of its own since then, outperforming the broader market across that span. The pharmaceutical company’s two flagship immunology drugs, Skyrizi and Rinvoq, have consistently exceeded expectations and face no U.S. patent expiration until at least 2033. That long runway gives AbbVie unusual earnings visibility for a large-cap drugmaker, along with time to develop new medicines that could sustain growth well beyond the current decade. AbbVie has demonstrated an ability to navigate patent cliffs without sacrificing dividend momentum, and the company has now raised its payout for 64 consecutive years when counting the time it operated under Abbott’s umbrella. Coca-Cola (NYSE: KO) rounds out the group with a similarly long dividend streak of 64 consecutive years, a figure that places it among the most consistent income generators in the entire equity market. The beverage giant has continued to deliver stability and a reliable income program even as consumers globally have faced persistent cost-of-living pressures and an uncertain macroeconomic backdrop. All three companies belong to the Dividend Kings, a designation reserved for corporations that have raised their dividends for at least 50 straight years, an elite threshold that fewer than a handful of businesses ever reach. What separates these three from the broader Dividend Kings universe is a combination of operational depth, market leadership, and the kind of structural advantages that tend to compound investor returns over very long holding periods. David Prior is a senior reporter at the Foreign Policy Journal, covering everything from current affairs and global politics to stock market news and analysis.
